newsitem.title: GREECE: Natl Bank/Greece to issue $200mln subordinated loan.
newsitem.headline: Natl Bank/Greece to issue $200mln subordinated loan.

text.p: State National Bank of Greece will issue a subordinated, callable loan up to $200 million with maturity up to 10 years in May or June 1997 following the approval by its general shareholders meeting today.

"The basic terms that can be specified today.. are that about $150-$200 million will be borrowed, the maturity of the loan will be 10 years and it will be issued in the euromarket," National Bank chairman Theodore Karatzas told shareholders.
The bank will reserve the right to call the floating-rate loan after five years, he said.

The subordinated eurodollar loan will be based on three- or six-month Libor plus an unspecified margin and will enhance the bank's capital adequacy and solvency ratios being classified as lower tier-II, he said.
"It will be the first entry of National Bank into international markets for a long-term loan after many years," said Karatzas.
National Bank of Greece picked Salomon Brothers and Chase Manhattan Bank to be lead underwriters for the issue.
